paragraphs: Tom sat at the desk in the living room. He had Dad's laptop in front of him. "I need the laptop for my homework," he said. Lily came in with Pip. "Tom, I want to play my pirate game," she said. "It's an app on this laptop." "Not now," said Tom. "My homework is about famous places in Thailand." "That's not fair!" said Lily. "I'm sorry, but my homework is for school," said Tom. Pip sat between them and looked at both of them.

Mom came in from the kitchen. "What's the matter?" she asked. "Tom has the laptop, and I want it," said Lily. "I need it for my homework," said Tom. "I have to draw a map of Thailand." "Can you draw a map?" asked Mom. "No," said Tom. "My map is bad." Pip walked on the paper, and Tom laughed. Lily laughed, too. "Now it's worse!" said Tom.

"My pirate game has a map of Thailand," said Lily. "It has famous places, too." "Really? Show me," said Tom. "Come and sit next to me," said Lily. Lily opened the app. "Look! Here's a famous beach, and here's an island," she said. "Your map is better than mine," said Tom. "Both of you can work on the laptop," said Mom. "Tom can write his homework, and Lily can find the treasure." Both children smiled. Tom wrote the names of the places on his paper. Lily played, and Pip slept on the sofa.
text.summary: Tom needs Dad's laptop for his homework, and Lily wants to play her pirate game on it. Mom helps them to work on it together.
